blocks.text: IdP attribute objects are reusable components that allow you to organize users based on their identity attributes. These objects use SAML attributes and SCIM data sourced from your identity provider (IdP) to define specific user populations. They are designed to shift policy creation from being network-centric to identity-centric, allowing you to build rules based on who the user is, not just their location. IdP attribute objects allow you to use a named object to define the user identity criteria when configuring VPN access policies.
Creating a library of IdP attribute objects provides the following benefits:

blocks.item: Centralize the management of user identity criteria. If the attributes defining a user group change, you only need to update the object, and all policies that reference it are automatically updated.
Simplify auditing and make policy rules self-documenting. A rule using a named object is easier to understand than manually configured SAML or SCIM attributes.

blocks.heading: About the IdP Attribute Object Page

blocks.text: On the IdP Attribute Object page (Private Access > VPN (for Legacy Apps) > VPN Access Policy IdP Address), you can do the following:

blocks.item: Search for an IdP attribute object by its name.
View a list of all configured IdP attribute objects. For each object, you can see:
Name: The name of the IdP attribute object.
Networks: The networks grouped in the IdP attribute object.
Modify the columns displayed in the table.
Display more rows or a different page of the table.
Go to the Access Policies page to view VPN access policy rules.
Go to the IP Address Object page to view IP address objects.
